title: Schematicity from the horizontal closure and infinitesimal special fibres
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $\pi$ generate its maximal ideal, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $Y$ be a separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that its diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $C\hookrightarrow Y$ be the closed subspace [def-sfb-space-closed-subspace] given by the schematic closure of $Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(R[1/\pi])$: on every etale affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$ its defining ideal is $\ker(B\to B[1/\pi])$. For every integer $n\geq1$, set $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(R/(\pi^n))$ and $Y_n=Y\times_SS_n$, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. If $C$ and all the algebraic spaces $Y_n$ are represented by schemes, then $Y$ is represented by an $S$-scheme. There is no group structure or flatness hypothesis on $Y$, and no single uniform exponent $n$ or global quasi-compactness is assumed.

source.place: Anantharaman, Schemas en groupes, espaces homogenes et espaces algebriques sur une base de dimension 1, Memoires SMF 33 (1973), Proposition 1.3.2 and its proof, printed pp.20-21 (OCR renders 1.3.2 as 1.5.2), using closed gluing of the flat closure with a sufficiently high infinitesimal fibre locally. Local archive WANTED; primary scan read at https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas of $Y$ and cover its source by affine open schemes $U_\alpha$. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], the image $V_\alpha\subseteq Y$ of each $U_\alpha$ is an open subspace, is quasi-compact, and has a surjective etale scheme cover; these images cover $Y$. Fix one nonempty $V=V_\alpha$. Its map to $S$ is quasi-compact in the sense used by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], namely after base change along every affine scheme $T\to S$: by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] the base change of the surjective etale $U_\alpha\to V$ along $V\times_ST\to V$ is a surjective etale map $U_\alpha\times_ST\to V\times_ST$, whose source is the affine scheme of a tensor product of rings over $R$; so $|V\times_ST|$ is quasi-compact by the last assertion of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. It has the locally finite type chart test of $Y$, so it is finite type [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. It is separated by restricting the given diagonal. In particular it is quasi-separated: on affine scheme tests its diagonal is a closed immersion, hence affine and quasi-compact by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; the affine base $S$ is separated. Every ideal of the DVR $R$ is principal, so $R$ is Noetherian [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and $S$ is Noetherian. The finite-type quasi-separated inheritance assertion of [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-acc], applied with base $S$, therefore makes $V$ Noetherian. This reduction never asserts quasi-compactness of $Y$.

source.place: Tag 04ZK, lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian; local reduction in Anantharaman Proposition 1.3.2.

proof.text: On $V$ let $\mathcal K_m=\ker(\pi^m:\mathcal O_V\to\mathcal O_V)$ for $m\geq1$. These are quasi-coherent ideals by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], since the structure module is locally free of rank one. They form an ascending chain. By [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-acc], there is $N\geq1$ with $\mathcal K_m=\mathcal K_N$ for all $m\geq N$. The ideal $\mathcal I$ of $C_V=C\times_YV$ is quasi-coherent and restricts on every etale affine chart to $\ker(B\to B[1/\pi])$ by the hypothesis and [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence]. Every element of this ring kernel is killed by some power of $\pi$, and conversely every such torsion element is in the kernel. Thus, checking on these charts, $\mathcal I=\mathcal K_N$ and $\pi^N\mathcal I=0$. The integer $N$ depends on $V$.

source.place: Tag 07UJ, lemma-acc-coherent; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1, lemma-properties-quasi-coherent; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MB, lemma-closed-immersion-ideals.

proof.text: Set $D=Y_N\times_YV$, whose ideal on every etale affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\to V$ is $\pi^NB$. The ideal correspondence [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence] identifies this with $\mathcal J=\pi^N\mathcal O_V$. If $x\in I_B\cap\pi^NB$, write $x=\pi^Nb$. Since $x$ is torsion, some $\pi^m x=0$, so $\pi^{m+N}b=0$. Hence $b\in I_B$ and step 2 gives $x=\pi^Nb=0$. This proves $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J=0$. Both $C_V$ and $D$ are schemes: they are the open subspaces induced by $V\hookrightarrow Y$ in the assumed schemes $C$ and $Y_N$. Their intersection $E=C_V\times_VD$ is a scheme, since it is the base change of the representable closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow V$ to the scheme $C_V$; both $E\to C_V$ and $E\to D$ are closed immersions, as can also be read from their quotient ideals on scheme tests.

source.place: Tag 03MB, lemma-closed-immersion-ideals; the torsion-intersection calculation is the elementary calculation of Anantharaman section 1.0 and Proposition 1.2.2(c).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] to the scheme diagram $C_V\leftarrow E\to D$. Its right map is integral: it is a closed immersion, so on affine tests the ring map is a quotient, and every element of the quotient satisfies the monic polynomial $T-a$ for a lift $a$. For each point of $D$ its fibre in $E$ is empty or one point. In the nonempty case its image in $C_V$ has an affine open neighbourhood; in the empty case take any affine open of $C_V$, allowing the empty affine if $C_V$ is empty. Thus the theorem's affine-neighbourhood hypothesis holds, and a scheme pushout $P=C_V\amalg_ED$ exists. By [lem-sfb-ferrand-pushout-space-agreement] this is also a pushout in algebraic spaces over $S$.

The ideal equality in step 3 permits [lem-sfb-closed-space-union-pushout] to be applied to $C_V,D\hookrightarrow V$. It makes $V$ a pushout of the same diagram in algebraic spaces. The two universal properties give maps $P\to V$ and $V\to P$ compatible with the inclusions of $C_V,D$. Each composite is the identity, since it and the identity agree on these two inclusions and the pushout extension is unique. Hence $V\simeq P$ is represented by an $S$-scheme. This holds for every $V_\alpha$. By [lem-sfb-space-largest-schematic-open], each $V_\alpha$ lies in the largest scheme open $Y_{\mathrm{sch}}$ of $Y$. Since their point images cover $Y$, this open has full point image and equals $Y$ by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. This proves the assertion, including the empty $Y$ case. Only local exponents $N$ have been used.
